# Dig, build & map
[textlink="Back to Mining & Industry" link="CMUGuideIndustry"]
[textlink="Shovels, pickaxes and powered tools: OOC controls" link="CMUGuideIndustryTools"]
## Pick the tool for the layer you enter
[bold]Hold tool → aim at nearby clear floor → [keybind="UseItemInHand"] → stay still.[/bold] Right-click the tool to switch between digging down and digging up. Walls, furniture and protected supports can block the route.
Large caverns begin at [bold]Z-3[/bold]. They can span several levels. Watch your step; the floor you see below may be a long way down.
## Leave yourself an exit
- Right-click a pit → [bold]Build[/bold]: one rope coil, or 25 steel for a ladder. - Open construction with [keybind="OpenCraftingMenu"] → [bold]Z-Level (Experimental)[/bold] for portable ladders and stairs. - A portable ladder needs a supporting wall or beam and an opening above. It cannot drill through a ceiling. - Support wide excavations with beams or pillars. Digging away the roof's support can cause a cave-in.
Hold a structural scanner and press [keybind="UseItemInHand"] to toggle its roof-stability overlay. Check support before widening a room. Click a ladder to climb; right-click it for the available climb and look directions. Open a closed hatch before trying again.
## Bring back knowledge, too
Nearby visible terrain is recorded as you explore underground. Make a [bold]cave survey map[/bold] from one paper in the construction menu; use [bold]Transcribe survey[/bold], then pass it to another explorer to read.
Reading maps combines their observations in the 3D tactical survey. Overlaps use the [bold]newest observation[/bold]. Survey knowledge lasts for this round.
[bold]Spectating?[/bold] Visit an underground level, then use your [bold]Mining map[/bold] action. Hit [bold]Refresh[/bold] after exploring further. A ghost's observations stay private; the normal tactical map still works separately.
